title: Autosculpt noisy-tenant fingerprint and reserve-rewind playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: After the 2026-02-15 capacity incident where a single tenant produced sustained KV cache churn and token-burst amplification, multiple dedicated clusters experienced degraded tail-latency and several soft evictions. Root cause: a combination of mis-sized reservations for long-tail tenants and uncontrolled short-lived burst tokens that allowed noisy workloads to monopolize aggregate GPU working set. This ticket defines an operational playbook ("autosculpt"), an automated fingerprinting pipeline for detecting noisy tenants early, and a non-disruptive "reserve-rewind" procedure to recover headroom without full evictions.
tasks: Implement lightweight tenant fingerprint exporter (telemetry) - capture per-tenant cache miss rate, average KV eviction rate, and burst token consumption (owner: Liam Chen, estimate: 3)
Prototype autosculpt policy: when fingerprint crosses severity threshold, reduce ephemeral burst allowance and apply soft reservation rewind (owner: Maya Ortiz, estimate: 2)
Add synthetic tenant workload generator for canary lanes to validate autosculpt decisions before global rollout (owner: Rajesh Nair, estimate: 2)
Create Grafana dashboard and alert rules: noisy-fingerprint-score, reserve-utilization-gap, soft-rewind-success (owner: SRE team, estimate: 1)
Update dedicated-runbook: include 'reserve-rewind' steps, safebackoff timings, and stakeholder notification template (owner: Ops Docs, estimate: 1)
Instrument audit trail for reserve-rewind actions to support rollback and post-action telemetry (owner: Liam Chen, estimate: 1)
Schedule game-day to exercise autosculpt in a staging cluster and measure false-positive/negative rates (owner: Maya Ortiz, estimate: 1)
Implement PR with feature flag gating and metrics (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/reproserv/pull/2149)
Coordinate with product to add customer-facing communication flow for planned soft-rewinds on Dedicated (owner: Nora Alvarez, estimate: 1)
Post-deploy retrospective and run-rate SLO analysis after two weeks in canary (owner: Ava Patel, estimate: 1)
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint exporter is running in canary and emits stable telemetry for 100% of requests in the canary shard
Autosculpt reduces burst allowance and triggers reserve-rewind without causing hard-evictions in 95% of simulated noisy events
Alerts fire with actionable signal (noisy-fingerprint-score) and include tenant id, score, and recent token consumption
Runbook includes clear rollback steps and escalation path; SRE runbook review approved
Customer communication flow template approved by PM and Legal
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Decided to prioritize non-disruptive mitigations (soft reserve rewinds) over immediate hard tenant ejections to avoid SLA violations (meeting notes: drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Aabc123)
2026-02-24: Chose fingerprint features: per-tenant KV eviction rate, prefix-cache-hit ratio, burst-token-rate, 95th/99th latency delta (discussion: #dedicated-capacity Slack thread)
2026-03-02: Opted for feature-flagged rollout with two canary clusters before org-wide activation (design doc: confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Autosculpt+Playbook)
2026-03-08: Agreed on conservative thresholds for initial canary to reduce false positives; will iterate based on game-day metrics
updates: 2026-02-19: Initial ticket created after postmortem synthesis. Action items consolidated from incident war room.
2026-02-25: Prototype telemetry agent merged into staging agent image (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/487). Basic metrics validated on a single pod.

2026-03-01: First autosculpt policy POC applied in staging; observed correct detection of synthetic noisy-worker but had a 12% false-positive in short burst scenarios. Lowered sensitivity and added short cooldown window.
2026-03-05: Added synthetic workload generator and ran 10 simulated scenarios; reserve-rewind prevented hard evictions in 9/10 cases. Documented failure mode for overlapping long-lived tenants.
2026-03-09: Grafana dashboard panels created (link below). Alert rules drafted and circulated for SRE review.
2026-03-10: Runbook draft submitted for review; Ops Docs requested clearer rollback timings and example Slack/PagerDuty messages. Assigned to Nora for communications draft.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: conservative thresholds may allow some noisy spikes to persist longer, but aggressive settings risk customer-visible evictions. We prioritize avoiding hard evictions for revenue-impacting tenants.
Tradeoff: fingerprinting increases telemetry cardinality; initial rollout will sample at 10% and backfill higher-rate sampling only for suspected shards to limit cost.
Consideration: long-lived model warmups can appear noisy. We'll add a startup dampening factor to the fingerprint to avoid penalizing legitimate warmup traffic.

Fallback: if autosculpt triggers unexpectedly, operators can run 'reserve-rewind rollback' which restores previous reservation state within 30s; metrics will indicate oscillation and trigger a manual pause
